bull.b: Rademikibart’s strong Phase 2 COPD results provide meaningful evidence of potential clinical differentiation in an important immune-mediated respiratory setting. If confirmed in later development, the reductions in treatment failure and exacerbations could support adoption and strengthen the company’s pipeline value.

The asthma program has advanced beyond early proof of concept, combining statistically significant lung-function improvement with a defined path toward Phase 3. Progress across asthma and COPD broadens the potential use of rademikibart and supports a more credible late-stage development strategy.

Very low debt limits interest obligations and reduces the balance-sheet burden associated with financing clinical development. This gives Connect more flexibility than a highly leveraged biotech, although its ability to fund operations still depends on cash resources and future capital access.

bear.b: The absence of reported 2025 revenue leaves Connect dependent on clinical progress rather than an established commercial base. Combined with a substantially larger net loss, this creates a weak earnings foundation and makes future financial performance highly dependent on successful product development.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means the company is consuming capital to advance its programs rather than funding development internally. Unless spending falls or revenue is rebuilt, continued clinical work will require external financing, increasing dilution and execution risk.

The sharp contraction in equity and total assets indicates that accumulated losses have materially reduced the resources supporting the business. A smaller capital base limits financial flexibility and may force Connect to raise funds on less favorable terms while it continues funding clinical development.
